answer.rationale: With expiry in 14 days, no auto-renew, incumbent refusing price movement, and the line at 94% with no buffer, a broad primary switch is the main TCO lever but carries unacceptable delivery risk before verification. I intend to qualify the low-cost vendor as a guarded second source rather than switch volume now: this should reduce single-source exposure, create credible cost pressure for the next review, and avoid interrupting committed volume. I want c2 checked because it supports fast low-cost onboarding and invoicing, and c3 because it supports second-source resilience under shortage conditions.
